items.title: Frank Amacker Interview, 1960-09-30
items.q: He played with Louis one time. He was the same man Louis Armstrong was in one time in Chicago. Johnny was, Johnny Sincere. And he was very popular in the band.

ctx.x: Now what about Johnny Sincere? Who did he play with?

He played with Louis one time. He was the same man Louis Armstrong was in one time in Chicago. Johnny was, Johnny Sincere. And he was very popular in the band. Johnny's quite a man. He's quite a band man, Johnny Sincere's, you know. He was quite a guitar. Of course his main way of making his living, I know you know that, but I tell you. The pleasure of living, you know. But he was quite an able man in the band, Johnny was, some years ago. Quite a guitar player.
Who did he play with down here? Do you remember?

items.title: Frank Amacker Interview, 1960-07-01
items.q: Johnny Sincere, he put two words to it. Johnny Sincere was one of the finest lyric writers I've ever heard of... because I played it, and Johnny Sincere, he worded it

ctx.x: Uh huh. But when did he write that down? About what time?

Oh, that was, oh let me see. I was about, let's see, that piece must be about 50, let's see. Oh, I was about, let's see. I was about, I was about 20, I was in some way in my, that's over 40 years ago, 40 years ago, that's over 40 years ago, around 50 years ago, not up in there. I was calling him a boy. I was sitting down one day, in Red Light District, just sitting down playing that melody. I was sitting down playing that melody, not knowing what I was playing. See? And he walked in and he says, gee what's that…
You got a killer? You got a killer? Your big E slept off the bridge
